bearings.rolling_load.title: Rolling-bearing equivalent dynamic load (P = X V Fr + Y Fa)

variables.name: V
variables.desc: rotation factor: 1 rotating inner ring, 1.2 rotating outer ring

assumptions: X, Y and V are catalogue values from the manufacturer (ISO 281): they depend on bearing type, the contact angle and the ratio Fa/Fr. V = 1 when the inner ring rotates, 1.2 when the outer ring rotates (shaft stationary).
method_references: Equivalent dynamic bearing load P = X V Fr + Y Fa (ISO 281; recalled)

bearings.bearing_life.title: Basic dynamic load rating: L10 life (millions of rev and hours)

variables.name: n
variables.desc: shaft speed in rev/s (enter rpm/60 or "1500 1/min")

variables.name: L10
variables.desc: rating life in millions of revolutions

procedure.python:
def _bearing_life(values):
    """Rating life L10 (millions of rev) and L10h (hours) from C, equivalent load P, exponent a, speed n.

    L10 = (C/P)^a with a = 3 (ball) or 10/3 (roller). L10h = L10 * 1e6 / (3600 * n) with n in rev/s (Hz).
    """
    C, P, a, n = values['C'], values['P'], values['a'], values['n']
    if P <= 0:
        raise MechError('P (equivalent dynamic load) must be positive')
    if n <= 0:
        raise MechError('n (speed) must be positive to convert life to hours')
    L10 = (C / P) ** a
    # 3600 is the s->h conversion so the output carries its declared unit 'h' (life in hours, the
    # engineering convention); n is rev/s (Hz), so L10*1e6/n is seconds.
    L10h = L10 * 1e6 / (3600.0 * n)
    return {'L10': L10, 'L10h': L10h}

assumptions: L10 = (C/P)^a in millions of revolutions (a = 3 ball, 10/3 roller). L10h = L10*1e6/(3600*n) with n in rev/s. Feed P from rolling_load; solve for C (bearing selection) by giving a target L10h. C and P must be in the same units.

bearings.bearing_reliability_life.title: Reliability-adjusted life (L_na = a1 * L10)

variables.name: a1
variables.desc: life adjustment factor for reliability (ISO 281 / catalogue)

method_references: Reliability-adjusted life L_na = a1 L10 (ISO 281; recalled)

bearings.weibull_reliability.title: Bearing reliability from three-parameter Weibull life distribution
assumptions: Three-parameter Weibull R = exp(-((L-x0)/(theta-x0))^b) for L >= x0 and theta > x0 (a MechError is raised otherwise, e.g. L = 1 with x0 = 2, theta = 1). x0, theta and b are INPUTS; commonly cited maker values are x0 = 0.02 L10, theta = 4.459 L10, b = 1.483 (recalled). At L = theta the reliability is e^-1 = 0.3679 for any b.
method_references: Weibull reliability distribution for bearing life (recalled)

bearings.static_load.title: Static load capacity and static safety factor (P0, s0 = C0/P0)
assumptions: ISO 76 equivalent static load P0 = max(X0 Fr + Y0 Fa, Fr): the larger of the combined term and the radial load alone, so P0 is never less than Fr (this is the binding case when the axial load is small or zero). X0, Y0, C0 are catalogue values. s0 = C0/P0 > 1 (typically 2+) for smooth operation.
method_references: Equivalent static bearing load P0 = max(X0 Fr + Y0 Fa, Fr) (ISO 76; recalled)

bearings.sommerfeld.title: Journal bearing Sommerfeld number (S = mu n (r/c)^2 / P)

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: lubricant dynamic viscosity at operating temperature (input)

variables.name: c
variables.desc: radial clearance (bearing radius minus journal radius)

variables.name: P
variables.desc: projected bearing pressure W/(2 r L)

assumptions: S is dimensionless. The relationship between S and the eccentricity ratio epsilon comes from the Raimondi–Boyd charts (NOT built in — see journal_min_film). Light loads (large S) are valid for the Petroff friction model.

bearings.petroff.title: Petroff friction coefficient and torque (light-load journal bearing)

variables.name: P
variables.desc: projected bearing pressure W/(2 r L)

assumptions: Petroff applies to lightly loaded (concentric, epsilon ~ 0) bearings: f = 2 pi^2 (mu n / P)(r / c). Equivalent torque form T_f = 4 pi^2 mu n r^3 L / c. For significant eccentricity use the Raimondi–Boyd friction variable (input).
method_references: Petroff equation for lightly loaded journal bearing friction (recalled)

bearings.journal_min_film.title: Minimum film thickness and eccentricity ratio (h0 = c(1 - epsilon))
assumptions: h0 = c - e = c(1 - epsilon) is the minimum film thickness at the point of closest approach. epsilon vs the Sommerfeld number S comes from the Raimondi–Boyd charts (input — not built in). Require h0 >= surface roughness to avoid metal contact.
method_references: Minimum film thickness h0 = c(1 - epsilon) (recalled)

bearings.journal_power_loss.title: Journal bearing friction power loss (H = f W 2 pi r n)

variables.name: f
variables.desc: coefficient of friction (from Petroff or Raimondi–Boyd input)

assumptions: H = T_f omega with T_f = f W r and omega = 2 pi n. The coefficient f may come from Petroff (light load) or the Raimondi–Boyd friction variable f (r/c) (input).
method_references: Power loss H = f W (2 pi r n) (recalled)

bearings.journal_temp_rise.title: Oil temperature rise across a bearing (dT = H / (rho cp Q))

variables.name: dT
variables.desc: lubricant temperature rise (delta; enter in K or delta_degC)

variables.name: H
variables.desc: heat to be carried away (friction power loss)

assumptions: Steady energy balance over the bearing: the heat generated is carried off by the oil flow, so dT = H/(rho cp Q). This form uses the total flow Q and neglects the side (leakage) flow; the Raimondi–Boyd correction for side flow is dT = H/(rho cp (Q - 0.5 Qs)) with Qs the side flow (input) — apply it when Qs/Q is significant. Aim for dT ~ 10–20 K across a bearing.
method_references: Energy balance H = rho cp Q dT (recalled)

bearings.journal_oil_flow.title: Journal bearing oil flow (Q = q* r c n L)

variables.name: q_f
variables.desc: dimensionless flow variable Q/(r c n L) (Raimondi–Boyd chart input)

assumptions: q_f = Q/(r c n L) is the dimensionless flow variable read from the Raimondi–Boyd charts at the operating S and L/D — an INPUT, not built in. The total flow feeds journal_temp_rise.
method_references: Dimensionless flow Q/(r c n L) (Raimondi–Boyd; recalled)

bearings.thrust_bearing_load.title: Thrust (collar/pivot) bearing load capacity (W = p_allow A)

variables.name: d_o
variables.desc: outer diameter of the thrust surface

variables.name: d_i
variables.desc: inner diameter (0 for a solid/pivot surface)

assumptions: Uniform pressure over the annular thrust face; p_allow is a table value for the material pair and duty (input). For rolling thrust bearings use bearing_life with the axial dynamic rating C_a and a = 10/3 (roller) or 3 (ball).
method_references: Thrust bearing capacity W = p_allow A, A = pi/4 (d_o^2 - d_i^2) (recalled)

source.derivation: L_na = a1*L10 = 0.62*1000 = 620 million rev (a1 = 0.62 is the ISO 281 factor for 95% reliability)

cases.classification: reference landmark; original citation confidence retained in source; not a certified external benchmark

source.ref: Landmark: at L = theta (with x0 = 0) the Weibull survival probability is R = e^-1 = 0.36788 for ANY shape b, because (L/theta)^b = 1. Not re-read; standard Weibull result.

source.derivation: R = e^-1 gives -ln R = 1, so (L - x0)/(theta - x0) = 1^(1/b) = 1 and L = theta = 1000
ISO 76 max: X0 Fr + Y0 Fa = 0.6*5000 + 0.5*0 = 3000 N < Fr = 5000 N, so P0 = max(3000, 5000) = 5000 N (the Fr branch of the max, the case the old formula got wrong); s0 = C0/P0 = 20000/5000 = 4
